correctness.rationale: A productive-simple-cycle least-common-multiple lemma proves the accepted unary length set eventually has the cycle LCM as period. The primitive prime-power period then divides this LCM, forcing one productive simple cycle of length divisible by the entire modulus. Bipartite underlying graphs force that non-loop cycle length to be even, giving the exact lower bound. Deterministic complete cycles of lengths m and lcm(m,2) attain the unrestricted and bipartite-cactus bounds. Enumeration subtracts all translation-invariant subsets and the 2m singleton/co-singleton controls. verify.py independently corroborates 935 primitive masks, 55,567 witness lengths and 214,660 small unary NFA candidates.

value.rationale: The originating structural regular-language theorem explicitly leaves quantitative state overhead open. For every prime-power modulus at least four, the new classification settles the exact overhead for 2^(p^k)-2^(p^(k-1))-2p^k genuinely multiresidue predicates, separating odd-prime and two-primary behavior and showing bipartite graphs and bipartite cacti have identical exact cost on this natural class. This is a complete infinite-family invariant with substantive model motivation, not a finite test or generic pumping exercise.
